_description: ContentForge Social Platform Specifications — Character limits, hashtag norms, voice guidelines, image/video specs, AI-disclosure requirements, and supported post types per platform. Used by the Social Adapter Agent (10-social-adapter) and cf-social-adapt skill. Every platform's verification date, review date and sources are in _provenance: a limit is only as current as its platform's entry there.
_posting_times_note: Posting-time folklore removed (July 2026); the old best_times/worst_times tables were unsourced and timezone-free. Use the brand's own platform analytics to determine posting windows.

_provenance._description: One entry per platform. status: read = the platform pages were read on verified_on; reported = a headline figure could not be read on a platform page and rests on a named secondary source or the platform's own announcement quoted elsewhere; carried = unchanged since an earlier pass and not re-read since. `reported` and `practice` list the fields that are not read figures: a practice field (hashtag counts, ideal lengths, the 1200-pixel image sizes) is an editorial recommendation, not a platform limit. review_by is the date a person must re-read the pages; a test fails if it is more than four months after verified_on. A second test fails from 30 days before any review_by, and after it, and a weekly job runs it, so the pages are read again while the limits are still trusted.

reported: format.truncation_point: no LinkedIn page states the see-more cut-off; secondary sources repeat about 210 characters on desktop and 140 on mobile
practice: image_specs.feed 1200x627 and image_specs.document 1080x1080 are recommendations inside LinkedIn's ranges, not figures on a LinkedIn page

reported: hashtags._note: the bar on hashtags in X ads from 2025-06-27 is reported by the press (2025-06-26), not stated on help.x.com
ai_disclosure: that X has no native AI label cannot be shown from a page
practice: image_specs.feed 1200x675 is inside X's 2:1 to 3:4 full-display range, not a stated size

reported: character_limit 63,206 and format.truncation_note about 477: no Meta page states either; socialk.it lists them (checked June 2026) and the first traces to a 2011 Facebook remark
image_specs.story: Meta states no video file size, so none is given
practice: hashtags: Facebook's hashtag help gives format rules, no count

reported: ai_disclosure: that Bluesky has no native AI label cannot be shown from a page
practice: image_specs.feed 1200x675 is inside the allowed range, not a stated size

hashtags.notes: Use industry-specific terms. Avoid overly generic hashtags. CamelCase for readability. The count is practice: LinkedIn gives none.

voice.notes: Write like a knowledgeable peer, not a press release. Conversational authority.

format._list_style_note: One item per line, optionally prefixed with a bullet character. Do NOT prefix list items with dashes — dash-prefixed lines read as em-dash overuse to the Phase 6.5 humanizer (catalog pattern 14).
format.truncation_note: LinkedIn shows roughly 140 (mobile) to 210 (desktop) characters before 'see more'. Hook must be in first 2 lines. LinkedIn publishes no see-more cut-off; these figures come from secondary sources, so treat them as practice.

feed._max_size_note: LinkedIn's photo page states 5 MB (help a527229); its media-types page gives a generic 100 MB and 36-megapixel cap for all media (a564109). 5 MB is the only figure stated for a photo in a post.

document._note: A LinkedIn document post takes PPT, PPTX, DOC, DOCX and PDF only (no PNG or JPG), and LinkedIn recommends PDF; animations render as static images and multi-layer PDFs must be flattened (help a518909, a564109). The 1080x1080 page size and 10-20 pages are practice, not LinkedIn limits.

multi_photo._note: A multi-photo post is a separate product from a document post: up to 20 photos at 5 MB each (help a527229).

ai_disclosure.mechanism: LinkedIn shows a C2PA icon automatically on image and video signed with C2PA Content Credentials (help a6282984); there is no manual label, and LinkedIn says it cannot yet label all AI-generated content, so for unsigned media disclose in post copy (e.g., 'Image: AI-generated')

linkedin.algorithm_notes: External links may reduce reach. Consider putting link in first comment. Native documents (carousels) get higher distribution.

twitter._limit_note: 280 characters for standard accounts; X Premium accounts can post up to 25,000 characters. Default adaptations should target the 280 limit unless the brand profile confirms a Premium account — and even then, short posts get better feed treatment. X's own pages disagree on the Premium limit: two say 25,000 (types of posts, X Premium) and one still says 4,000 (how to post). Counting is weighted: emoji and CJK characters count 2.

hashtags._note: X recommends no more than 2 hashtags per post as best practice, though you may use as many as you like (help.x.com, 2026-09-28). Hashtags have been barred from X ads since 2025-06-27 (press reports, not on help.x.com). Zero hashtags is a legitimate default for an organic post; use 1-2 only when a specific tag has an active audience.
hashtags.notes: Hashtags consume character budget. Use only high-value, specific hashtags. Never in mid-sentence.

voice.notes: Every word must earn its place. One idea per tweet. Be sharp.

format.truncation_note: URLs always count as 23 characters regardless of actual length.

feed._note: X accepts GIF, JPEG and PNG files and no other format (help.x.com, 2026-09-28). Photos up to 5 MB; animated GIFs up to 5 MB on mobile and 15 MB on web. A single photo between 2:1 and 3:4 displays in full; 1200x675 is practice inside that range.

ai_disclosure.mechanism: none native — disclose manually in post copy

twitter.algorithm_notes: Replies and quote tweets boost distribution. Threads get more sustained visibility than single tweets.

hashtags.notes: Instagram allows up to 5 hashtags in a reel or post: announced by Instagram's verified @creators account on Threads, 2025-12-18 ("Starting today, Instagram will allow up to 5 hashtags in a reel or post"); the Help Center page could not be read, so treat 5 as the cap. Mix one broad reach tag with specific and niche discovery tags. Avoid banned hashtags. Put them at the end of the caption: whether hashtags in a first comment count toward the cap is not documented.

voice.notes: The visual does the heavy lifting. Caption adds context and personality. Write like you are talking to a friend who is interested in the topic.

format.truncation_note: Instagram shows ~125 characters before 'more'. First line is critical.

reel._note: Instagram lets accounts record and edit reels up to 20 minutes (reported; the rollout varies by account and by upload route, and a camera-roll upload is reported at 15), and reels over 3 minutes are not recommended to new audiences, so keep a reel for reach to 180 seconds or less. Stories remain 60s per card.

carousel._max_slides_note: Instagram raised the carousel ceiling to 20 slides (from 10) in 2025. ~10 slides remains the practical engagement ceiling — completion rates fall off sharply beyond that.

ai_disclosure.mechanism: Meta 'AI info' label — auto-applied to detected synthetic media; disclose proactively via the AI label toggle when posting photorealistic AI content

instagram.algorithm_notes: Carousels get highest engagement. Saves and shares weight more than likes. Reels get broader distribution than feed posts. Alt text improves accessibility and may boost SEO.

facebook._limit_note: Reported, not read: no Meta page states a post character limit. 63,206 comes from socialk.it (checked June 2026) and traces to a 2011 Facebook remark.

hashtags.notes: Hashtags are less important on Facebook. Use 1-3 relevant ones. Do not overdo it. The count is practice: Facebook's help gives format rules, no number.

voice.notes: Write for a broad audience. Stories and questions outperform link dumps. Make people feel invited to participate.

format.truncation_note: Facebook truncates around 477 characters with 'See more'. Hook in first paragraph. Meta states no cut-off; about 477 characters on desktop is reported by socialk.it (June 2026).

feed._max_size_note: Graph API photo uploads cannot exceed 10 MB, and Meta recommends PNG files stay under 1 MB. Link-preview images cannot exceed 8 MB (Images in Link Shares); 1200x630 at 1.91:1 is Meta's minimum for a large preview.

story._note: Page Stories API: photos up to 10 MB; MP4 video 3 to 90 seconds at 9:16, 1080x1920 recommended and 540x960 minimum; a reel published as a story cannot exceed 60 seconds. Meta states no video file size (an earlier 250 MB figure had no source).

ai_disclosure.mechanism: Meta 'AI info' label: applied when Meta detects industry-standard AI image indicators or when the poster discloses; AI-generated content keeps the visible label and content only edited by AI carries it in the post menu. Meta requires its disclosure tool for organic photorealistic video or realistic-sounding audio that was digitally created or altered, and may apply penalties if it is skipped, so disclose proactively when posting photorealistic AI content

facebook.algorithm_notes: Comments weight heavily in algorithm. Questions and polls drive comments. Native images and video outperform external links. Engagement bait ('tag a friend') is penalized.

hashtags.notes: Threads allows ONE topic tag per post (Meta's Threads API page, read 2026-10-27: "Only one topic tag is allowed per post"). Threads culture is less hashtag-driven. Keep it natural. Topic tags render without the # symbol.

voice.notes: Write like texting a smart colleague. Hot takes, quick insights, and genuine questions perform best. Authenticity over polish.

format.truncation_note: No truncation at 500 chars. Full post visible.

ai_disclosure.mechanism: Meta 'AI info' label (same system as Instagram/Facebook)

threads.algorithm_notes: Replies and conversation threads get amplified. Text-only posts perform well. Images optional but not required. Authenticity and opinion drive engagement.

tiktok._limit_note: Caption limit for video posts and photo posts. Keep the first ~100 characters hook-worthy; captions truncate in feed. Sources split between 2,200 and 4,000 characters and no TikTok page could be read for this check: 2,200 is the safe value until a caption is checked in the app.

hashtags.notes: Mix one broad tag, 2-3 niche/topic tags, and optionally one branded tag. TikTok search behaves like a search engine — keyword-rich captions matter as much as hashtags.

voice.notes: Lead with the payoff in the first second. Text overlays carry the message for sound-off viewers. Polished brand voice underperforms creator-style delivery.

format.truncation_note: Feed shows roughly the first 1-2 lines of caption before 'more'.

feed_video._note: Uploads up to 10 minutes supported; short (under 60s) videos still get the widest distribution.

photo_post._note: TikTok photo posts (carousel photo mode) support up to 35 images with music. Strong format for step-by-step and listicle repurposing.

ai_disclosure.mechanism: TikTok 'AI-generated content' toggle at upload — required by TikTok policy for realistic synthetic media; unlabeled AI content risks removal

tiktok.algorithm_notes: Completion rate and rewatches dominate distribution. Photo posts get carousel-style swipe engagement. Native text overlays and trending audio boost reach. Watermarked reposts from other platforms are penalized.

bluesky._limit_note: 300 graphemes: the post lexicon caps text at maxGraphemes 300 and, separately, 3,000 bytes (app.bsky.feed.post).

hashtags.notes: Hashtags are clickable but carry no native algorithmic boost — discovery runs on custom feeds and keyword search. Write for search terms, not tags. The count is practice: Bluesky states none.

avoid: cross-posted X threads with X conventions
voice.notes: Bluesky culture is anti-broadcast and skeptical of brands. Conversational, useful, and self-aware posts earn replies; hard selling gets muted.

format.truncation_note: No mid-post truncation at 300 chars. Links render as social cards (title + image pulled from OG tags) and do not consume extra characters beyond the URL text.

feed._max_size_note: The app.bsky.embed.images lexicon allows 2,000,000 bytes per image (formerly 1 MB; atproto PR #4823, merged 2026-04-08) and accepts any image type; the maintainers' 2026-04-07 announcement allows up to 4000x4000 pixels. Up to 4 images per post. 1200x675 is practice.

ai_disclosure.mechanism: none native — disclose manually in post copy or alt text

bluesky.algorithm_notes: No single master algorithm — users subscribe to custom feeds. Getting picked up by topical feeds (via keywords) matters more than posting time. Alt text is strongly normed; posts without it get called out.

youtube_shorts._limit_note: Title caps at 100 characters. Description allows 5,000 but only the first ~100 characters show without expansion — front-load the hook and keywords.

ideal_length._note: Applies to the description. Titles should be 40-70 characters for full display on all surfaces.

hashtags.notes: #Shorts is no longer required for classification. Use 1-3 topical tags; YouTube search keywords in the title and description matter far more.

avoid: clickbait that the video doesn't pay off
voice.notes: The title is the hook. Front-load the topic keyword for search. Shorts viewers decide in under 2 seconds.

format.truncation_note: Description truncates at ~100 visible characters; links below the fold still count for click-through from the expanded view.

short._note: Shorts support up to 3 minutes (raised from 60s in October 2024). Under-60s Shorts still see the strongest swipe-feed distribution.

ai_disclosure.mechanism: YouTube 'altered or synthetic content' disclosure at upload — required for realistic AI-generated or altered media; YouTube may add the label itself if undisclosed

youtube_shorts.algorithm_notes: Swipe-through rate and viewed-vs-swiped ratio drive distribution. Shorts feed traffic dwarfs search for this format, but titles still index in YouTube search. Loopable endings increase rewatch rate.

hashtag_tiers._description: Hashtag categorization framework used across all platforms

tier_1_broad.description: High volume, high competition industry hashtags

tier_2_specific.description: Medium volume, medium competition topic hashtags

tier_3_niche.description: Low volume, low competition, high relevance hashtags
tier_3_niche.use_case: Niche audience engagement, thought leadership positioning

post_frameworks._description: Five core post frameworks referenced by templates/social-post-templates.md
post_frameworks.announcement: Announce a key finding or trend with context and CTA
post_frameworks.data_driven_insight: Lead with a specific statistic, provide analysis, end with implication
post_frameworks.how_to_tip: Practical step-by-step value the reader can act on immediately
post_frameworks.quote_highlight: Feature a quotable line with attribution and commentary
post_frameworks.story_case_study: Narrative arc: problem, solution, result with real-world proof
